site.name: OIC from Scratch
site.author: @devwithprabir
site.tagline: Learn Oracle Integration Cloud from zero, one hand-written page at a time.

notes.title: How Systems Talk
notes.summary: How one system talks to another: the restaurant, the contact list, the postal address, the bank and the hotel, all the way to how OIC uses them.

notes.title: Data Formats
notes.summary: Open the parcel: JSON and XML explained with contact cards, labelled jars and bank forms, then XSD rules, XPath paths and XSLT recipes, the things OIC’s mapper runs on.

notes.title: 3.1 · REST in depth
notes.summary: A REST call read line by line: raw HTTP, address design, methods and their answers, the four places for data, headers, Content-Type vs Accept, error bodies, statelessness, ETags, versioning, OpenAPI and webhooks.

notes.title: 3.2 · SOAP & WSDL in depth
notes.summary: Take a real WSDL apart section by section, follow its reference chain to the Body, and master SOAP 1.1 vs 1.2, SOAPAction, faults, WS-Security and Oracle Fusion’s SOAP services.

notes.title: 3.3 · API security in depth
notes.summary: The exact requests behind Basic Auth, API keys, OAuth 2.0 client credentials and authorization code, refresh tokens, scopes, JWT claims and signatures, OCI IAM, and OIC’s security policies.

notes.title: 3.4 · Real-world APIs
notes.summary: Survive real APIs: reading docs, pagination, filtering, Oracle Fusion REST anatomy and query parameters, rate limits, retries with backoff, idempotency, timeouts, async jobs, and Postman tests and runners.

notes.title: 4.2 · Joins, grouping & changing data
notes.summary: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL and self joins, aggregates with GROUP BY and HAVING, the order a query really runs, subqueries, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, transactions, idempotent MERGE, sequences, views and indexes.

notes.title: 4.3 · PL/SQL & databases in OIC
notes.summary: PL/SQL blocks, variables, loops, exceptions, procedures, functions and packages, a real staging-table loader, JSON in SQL, and exactly how OIC’s database adapters connect, call procedures, run SQL and poll tables.

notes.title: 4.1 · What is a database?
notes.summary: For complete beginners: what data is, why companies move from registers and Excel to databases, what a table looks like inside, primary and foreign keys, the rules that guard data, NULL, and your very first SQL query, word by word.

notes.title: 6.1 · What is OIC?
notes.summary: Why companies need integration, point-to-point vs a hub, the 8 core OIC words, one integration step by step, where OIC lives in Oracle Cloud, editions, roles, getting your own instance, and a full console tour.

notes.title: 6.2 · Connections & adapters
notes.summary: Adapter vs connection, kinds of adapters, trigger and invoke roles, the five parts of every connection, building your first REST invoke and trigger connections click by click, security policies, access types and the connectivity agent.

notes.title: 6.3 · Your first integration
notes.summary: Build a working REST-to-REST integration click by click: integration styles, the canvas, the endpoint wizard, sample JSON, the mapper, business identifiers, then activate it and get your first 200 response.
